advisor_identified: Historian of North American cultural history and Cold War cultural diplomacy at Concordia University; supervisor of Eric Fillion’s 2019 history PhD.

doctorate.title: English-Canadian Literary Culture in the Modernist Milieu, 1920-40

evidence.says: Concordia’s repository identifies Eric Fillion’s Experiments in Cultural Diplomacy: Music as Mediation in Canadian-Brazilian Relations (1940s-1960s) as a 2019 history PhD and lists Carr, Graham as thesis supervisor.
Faculty profile identifies Carr as a professor of history, describes his research in cultural diplomacy and the Cold War, and lists a PhD from the University of Maine.
Concordia’s appointment announcement states that Carr joined its Department of History in 1983 after earning his PhD from the University of Maine.

The works cited in Colin Hill’s Generic Experiment and Confusion in Early Canadian Novels of the Great War lists Graham Carr’s English-Canadian Literary Culture in the Modernist Milieu, 1920-40 as a University of Maine dissertation, 1983.

notes: The linked record matches the author, institution, year and dissertation topic. Its title omits the word Literary, which appears in the published dissertation citation. Title and year are supported by a scholarly bibliography rather than a thesis catalogue.
